messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
We need to perform t-test on two independent samples. We have dataset A: [12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35] (n=10). Dataset B: [14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36] (n=10). We need to compute t-statistic and p-value for alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01. Use two-sided test? Usually t-test. We'll compute mean, variance, pooled variance, t-statistic. Let's compute.

Dataset A: sum = 12+15+18+20+22+25+28+30+32+35 = let's sum: 12+15=27; +18=45; +20=65; +22=87; +25=112; +28=140; +30=170; +32=202; +35=237. So mean_A = 237/10 = 23.7.

Compute squared deviations: (12-23.7)^2 = (-11.7)^2 = 136.89. (15-23.7)=-8.7^2=75.69. (18-23.7)=-5.7^2=32.49. (20-23.7)=-3.7^2=13.69. (22-23.7)=-1.7^2=2.89. (25-23.7)=1.3^2=1.69. (28-23.7)=4.3^2=18.49. (30-23.7)=6.3^2=39.69. (32-23.7)=8.3^2=68.89. (35-23.7)=11.3^2=127.69. Sum of squares = let's add: 136.89+75.69=212.58; +32.49=245.07; +13.69=258.76; +2.89=261.65; +1.69=263.34; +18.49=281.83; +39.69=321.52; +68.89=390.41; +127.69=518.10. So variance_A = sum/(n-1)=518.10/9=57.5667. Standard deviation_A = sqrt(57.5667)=7.590.

Dataset B: sum = 14+17+19+21+23+26+29+31+33+36 = let's sum: 14+17=31; +19=50; +21=71; +23=94; +26=120; +29=149; +31=180; +33=213; +36=249. Mean_B = 249/10 = 24.9.

Squared deviations: (14-24.9)=-10.9^2=118.81. (17-24.9)=-7.9^2=62.41. (19-24.9)=-5.9^2=34.81. (21-24.9)=-3.9^2=15.21. (23-24.9)=-1.9^2=3.61. (26-24.9)=1.1^2=1.21. (29-24.9)=4.1^2=16.81. (31-24.9)=6.1^2=37.21. (33-24.9)=8.1^2=65.61. (36-24.9)=11.1^2=123.21. Sum: 118.81+62.41=181.22; +34.81=216.03; +15.21=231.24; +3.61=234.85; +1.21=236.06; +16.81=252.87; +37.21=290.08; +65.61=355.69; +123.21=478.90. Variance_B = 478.90/9=53.2111. SD_B = sqrt(53.2111)=7.292.

Now compute pooled variance: sp^2 = ((n1-1)*s1^2 + (n2-1)*s2^2)/(n1+n2-2) = (9*57.5667 + 9*53.2111)/18 = (517.1003 + 478.8999)/18 = 995.0002/18 = 55.2778. So sp = sqrt(55.2778)=7.433.

Standard error of difference: SE = sp * sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) = 7.433 * sqrt(0.1 + 0.1) = 7.433 * sqrt(0.2) = 7.433 * 0.4472136 = 3.322.

t-statistic = (mean_A - mean_B)/SE = (23.7 - 24.9)/3.322 = (-1.2)/3.322 = -0.3615. Absolute t = 0.3615.

Degrees of freedom = n1+n2-2 = 18.

Now we need p-value for two-sided test. For df=18, t=0.3615. The p-value is 2*(1 - CDF(|t|)). For small t, p-value will be large. Let's approximate using t distribution. For df=18, t=0.3615, the two-tailed p-value ~ 0.72? Let's compute more precisely. Use approximate formula: For t=0.3615, the cumulative probability at t is about 0.641? Actually t=0.3615 is small, so CDF ~ 0.641? Wait t=0.3615 corresponds to about 0.641? Let's approximate using standard normal: z=0.3615, CDF=0.641. But t with df=18 has heavier tails, so CDF maybe slightly lower, maybe 0.638. So 1-CDF ~ 0.362. Then two-tailed p ~ 0.724. So p > 0.05 and > 0.01. So fail to reject null at both levels.

But we can compute more accurate using t distribution tables or approximate. Let's approximate using t distribution: For df=18, t=0.3615, the two-tailed p-value is about 0.72. So we can state p ≈ 0.72.

Thus at alpha=0.05 and 0.01, we do not reject null; means are not significantly different.
